title: Oliver Cowdery already had a witness: peace from God
setting: Oliver Cowdery had boarded with Joseph Smith’s parents near Palmyra, New York. Joseph’s history says Oliver prayed there about the plates and received a confirmation. He arrived in Harmony, Pennsylvania, on 5 April 1829 and began writing as Joseph translated two days later. Some time after, Joseph dictated this revelation, which the heading says came through the Urim and Thummim. It seems to have answered questions Oliver had not voiced to Joseph.
summary: The revelation announces a marvelous work and calls anyone who desires to reap in a ripe field. It tells Oliver to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It tells him to stand by Joseph, to admonish him, and to accept admonition from him. It reminds him that each time he inquired, the Spirit instructed him. It points him to a night when he prayed and received peace in his mind. It offers him a gift to translate, like Joseph, and gives both of them the keys of this gift. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice tells them to fear not and do good. It ends by asking them to look to him in every thought and behold his wounds.

contextNote.title: A witness Oliver had already received
contextNote.text: Oliver wanted more assurance that the work was true. Verse 22 sends him back to the night he “cried unto me in your heart” for an answer. Verse 23 then asks what greater witness he could have than peace from God. Verse 24 adds a second sign: the revelation told him “things which no man knoweth” about himself. David Whitmer later recalled Oliver writing that Joseph had revealed things only God could know. In this section, a witness is peace spoken to the mind, confirmed by private knowledge.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 6–9 teaches that Heavenly Father speaks to us through the Holy Ghost. In verses 14–16 and 22–23, what forms did the Lord’s answers to Oliver take?
reviewNote: Read all 37 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, April 1829, to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery, with Oliver beginning as scribe on 7 April. JSP historical introduction read for Oliver’s boarding with the Smiths, his prior confirmation, the 5 April arrival, David Whitmer’s recollection, and the unknown exact date. David Whitmer is included because the contextNote cites his recollection. Fact-check 2026-10-12: setting now attributes the Urim and Thummim method to the heading instead of stating it as fact.
